objective: Relate local domain geometry to hybrid labels, count sigma and pi bonds, and explain restricted rotation.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.md: Count all local domains before naming a hybridization. A double bond includes one sigma bond. A lone pair counts as a domain even though it does not make a bond.

blocks.title: Exam practice
blocks.md: Check each highlighted atom independently. For molecule-wide sigma counts, also count terminal atom bonds.

blocks.title: Hybridization, sigma bonds and pi bonds
blocks.focus: Count local domains and mark which bonds require unhybridized p orbitals.

blocks.title: Ethene
blocks.problem: For $\ce{H2C=CH2}$, identify both carbon hybrid labels and count all $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds.
blocks.answer: Both C atoms are $sp^2$; total $5\sigma$ and $1\pi$.

steps.title: Count domains
steps.md: Each C has two C–H directions and one C–C direction.
steps.why: The double bond counts as one domain.

steps.title: Count overlaps
steps.md: Four C–H and one C–C sigma bond give five. One p orbital on each C forms the pi bond.
steps.why: Extra bond order comes from side-on overlap.

blocks.title: Two different carbon centers
blocks.problem: For $\ce{CH3-C#N}$, identify both carbon hybrid labels.
blocks.answer: Methyl C is $sp^3$ and nitrile C is $sp$.

steps.title: At methyl C
steps.md: Three H neighbors plus the nitrile C give four directions.

steps.title: At nitrile C
steps.md: It has one C neighbor and one N neighbor, giving two directions.
steps.why: Two unhybridized p orbitals supply the two pi bonds to N.
